physicians-surgeons.headline: Play physicians and surgeons: the longest ladder, the highest ceiling
physicians-surgeons.whoItsFor: People committed to an 11-15 year training runway who want the highest verified BLS median and the top clinical ceiling in this batch.
physicians-surgeons.firstDollar: 11-15 years. Attending-level pay doesn't start until residency (sometimes fellowship) is complete; residency itself pays roughly $60-70K/yr as a trainee wage, not attending income.

steps.title: 1. Pre-med foundation (undergrad + MCAT)
steps.body: Bachelor's degree with pre-med coursework (biology, chemistry, organic chem, physics), a competitive GPA, and the MCAT. ~4 years.

steps.title: 2. Medical school (MD or DO)
steps.body: Apply via AMCAS or AACOMAS, complete a 4-year MD or DO program, pass USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK (or COMLEX for DO).

steps.title: 3. Match into residency
steps.body: Rank programs through the NRMP Match, then complete residency: 3 years for primary care/family medicine up to 5-7 years for surgical subspecialties, at trainee pay.

steps.title: 4. Optional fellowship for subspecialty
steps.body: 1-3 more years for cardiology, ortho subspecialties, and similar, which push income well past the broad median.

steps.title: 5. Licensure and first attending job
steps.body: Pass USMLE Step 3 (or COMLEX Level 3), get a state medical license, credential with a hospital or group, and negotiate the first attending contract.

pitfalls: Six-figure med school debt compounding through a low-pay residency
Choosing a specialty for prestige rather than fit and lifestyle
Skipping contract review on the first attending job, RVU structures and non-competes vary wildly
Underestimating years to breakeven against non-medical peers who started earning at 22

airline-pilots.headline: Play airline pilots: buy the flight hours, earn the seniority
airline-pilots.whoItsFor: People willing to front real training capital for a defined, checkbox-style path to a six-figure, seniority-driven career.
airline-pilots.firstDollar: First paid flying job (flight instructor or regional first officer) can come in 1.5-2 years once you hold a commercial certificate; the 1,500-hour ATP threshold for an airline seat typically takes 2-3 years total.

steps.title: 1. Private and instrument ratings
steps.body: Start flight training at a Part 61/141 school or a collegiate aviation program, earn a Private Pilot Certificate then an Instrument Rating. Roughly $15-25K.

steps.title: 2. Commercial certificate + CFI
steps.body: Add a Commercial Pilot Certificate and, usually, a Certified Flight Instructor rating so you can build hours by teaching. Another $20-30K.

steps.title: 3. Build the 1,500 hours
steps.body: Fly as a CFI, banner tow, aerial survey, or similar to accumulate the FAA-mandated 1,500 hours for an ATP certificate (250 hours with an approved bachelor's under R-ATP rules).

steps.title: 4. Earn the ATP certificate, get hired regional
steps.body: Pass the ATP written and checkride, apply to regional carriers (Envoy, SkyWest, PSA, and similar), complete type-rating training.

steps.title: 5. Build seniority toward a major
steps.body: Regional first officer pay is modest; seniority (years of service, base, aircraft) at a major carrier is what drives pay past $300-400K for senior captains.

tools: FAA written test prep (Sheppard Air, Sporty's)
pitfalls: Financing $80-100K+ in flight training debt before any airline income starts
Treating regional first-officer pay (often under $60K to start) as the ceiling instead of the on-ramp
Ignoring commuting, base, and seniority mechanics that dominate quality of life and pay progression

dentists.headline: Play dentists: license once, then buy or build the practice
dentists.whoItsFor: People who want a licensed clinical ceiling with a well-trodden path to practice ownership.
dentists.firstDollar: ~8 years to first income as an associate dentist; ownership, buying into or starting a practice, is what pushes pay meaningfully above the employee median.

steps.title: 1. Pre-dental undergrad + DAT
steps.body: Bachelor's degree with pre-dental science coursework, a competitive GPA, and the Dental Admission Test (DAT).

steps.title: 2. Dental school (DDS or DMD)
steps.body: 4-year CODA-accredited program, with clinical rotations in years 3-4.

steps.title: 3. Pass licensure exams
steps.body: The National Board Dental Examination (INBDE) plus a state or regional clinical licensure exam.

steps.title: 4. Associate at an existing practice
steps.body: Most new dentists start as an associate, commission or salary plus production bonus, to build clinical speed and a patient base before owning.

steps.title: 5. Buy in or start a practice
steps.body: Use a practice-acquisition loan (several banks specialize in dental practice lending) to buy an existing book or start fresh; ownership is where income clears $250K+.

tools: Dental-specific practice lenders (Bank of America Practice Solutions, Live Oak Bank)
pitfalls: Dental school debt averaging $300K+ that eats years of associate-level pay
Buying a practice at an inflated multiple without a broker/CPA review
Underestimating the non-clinical skills, staffing, billing, marketing, that practice ownership actually requires

financial-managers.headline: Play financial managers: climb from analyst to the office that signs the checks
financial-managers.whoItsFor: Finance and accounting grads willing to spend 5-10 years building a track record before stepping into a controller, treasurer, or finance-director seat.
financial-managers.firstDollar: ~7 years. This is a promotion-path deck, not a licensing-gate one: the credential (CPA/CFA/MBA) matters less than the years of P&L, FP&A, or accounting ownership behind you.

steps.title: 1. Finance/accounting/business bachelor's
steps.body: Build the technical base, accounting, corporate finance, financial modeling, that every finance-manager track requires.

steps.title: 2. Entry analyst role
steps.body: Start as a financial, staff, or FP&A analyst at a company, or in public accounting (Big 4 audit is a common on-ramp).

steps.title: 3. Earn a credential that signals depth
steps.body: A CPA license (accounting track) or CFA charter (investment/analysis track) is the single biggest lever for promotion speed; both take 1-3 years alongside work.

steps.title: 4. Move into a management layer
steps.body: Progress from analyst to senior analyst to manager, owning a budget, a close process, or a business unit's numbers, typically 5+ years in.

steps.title: 5. Step into a financial-manager title
steps.body: Controller, treasurer, or finance director, often via internal promotion or a lateral move; an MBA can accelerate this jump but is optional.

tools: Financial modeling courses (Wall Street Prep, CFI)
pitfalls: Treating the CPA/CFA as optional when it's the fastest credential-based promotion lever available
Staying too long in a pure-analyst role without asking for P&L or team ownership
Switching companies too often to build the multi-year track record promotion committees actually look for

lawyers.headline: Play lawyers: pass the bar, then pick BigLaw scale or small-firm ceiling
lawyers.whoItsFor: People willing to take on law-school debt for a genuinely bimodal market: BigLaw associate pay starts near $225K, but most lawyers earn well under the reported median.
lawyers.firstDollar: ~7 years to first income as a licensed, practicing attorney; a strong 2L-year summer associate offer can convert to real BigLaw pay before graduation.

steps.title: 1. Bachelor's degree + LSAT
steps.body: Any major works; build a competitive GPA and LSAT score, since both drive law school admission and scholarship money.

steps.title: 2. Law school (JD, 3 years)
steps.body: Attend an ABA-accredited program; 1L grades and law review/journal placement heavily influence which firms recruit you.

steps.title: 3. Summer associate recruiting (OCI)
steps.body: On-campus interviewing after 1L or 2L year is the main pipeline into BigLaw; a strong summer associate offer often converts to a full-time job.

steps.title: 4. Pass the bar exam
steps.body: Sit for the bar in the state you intend to practice (the UBE is portable across many states); this is the hard gate to practicing law at all.

steps.title: 5. Choose the track
steps.body: BigLaw associate (highest pay, longest hours, up-or-out to partner), government/public-interest (lower pay, PSLF loan forgiveness eligible), or small-firm/solo (income depends entirely on business development).

pitfalls: Attending a low-ranked law school on debt without a scholarship
Assuming the reported median applies broadly when the market is genuinely bimodal, BigLaw vs. everyone else
Missing PSLF-track loan forgiveness by leaving public-interest work before the 10-year clock completes

ai-ml-engineers.headline: Play AI/ML engineer: the research-adjacent track above general software dev
ai-ml-engineers.whoItsFor: Strong CS builders willing to go deep on math and ML fundamentals instead of stopping at general software engineering.
ai-ml-engineers.firstDollar: ~9 years on the BLS-tracked path (bachelor's plus graduate research background); in practice, many working ML engineers enter industry with a strong bachelor's plus a portfolio of shipped models, no PhD required for most roles.

steps.title: 1. CS/math foundation
steps.body: Bachelor's in computer science, math, or a related quantitative field; linear algebra, probability, and algorithms are the load-bearing courses.

steps.title: 2. Build a real ML portfolio
steps.body: Ship actual models, not tutorials: a Kaggle competition result, a fine-tuned open-source model, a deployed inference pipeline. This substitutes for credentials at most companies.

steps.title: 3. Go deep with a master's or equivalent self-study
steps.body: A master's in CS/ML (or the BLS-tracked PhD for pure research-scientist roles) sharpens the theory; many industry ML engineer roles hire strong bachelor's-plus-portfolio candidates without it.

steps.title: 4. Target ML-specific interview loops
steps.body: These test differently from general SWE, ML system design, applied math, take-home modeling tasks, not just algorithm puzzles.

steps.title: 5. Specialize to raise the ceiling
steps.body: NLP/LLMs, computer vision, or ML infra/MLOps are the sub-tracks that command the highest total comp at AI labs and large tech companies, well above the broad BLS median.

tools: fast.ai or Andrew Ng's ML courses
GPU cloud for training runs (Lambda, RunPod)
pitfalls: Confusing 'took an ML course' with 'shipped a model that works on real data'
Chasing PhD-only research roles when most paying ML engineer jobs need a bachelor's plus proof of work
Ignoring that the BLS median badly understates top-of-market AI-lab total comp, it's capped at the broad occupational category

petroleum-engineers.headline: Play petroleum engineers: one degree, a commodity-cycle ceiling
petroleum-engineers.whoItsFor: Engineering students willing to bet on energy-sector demand and geographic concentration for one of the fastest, highest-paying engineering on-ramps.
petroleum-engineers.firstDollar: ~4 years, the shortest time-to-first-income in this batch. A first job out of a petroleum engineering bachelor's pays well above the general engineering median.

steps.title: 1. ABET-accredited petroleum engineering bachelor's
steps.body: A small number of schools offer the specific degree (Texas A&M, UT Austin, Colorado School of Mines, Oklahoma, LSU); a mechanical or chemical engineering degree with an energy focus is a viable alternative entry.

steps.title: 2. Internship with an operator or service company
steps.body: Summer internships at majors (ExxonMobil, Chevron) or service companies (SLB, Halliburton, Baker Hughes) are the standard hiring pipeline into full-time roles.

steps.title: 3. First role as a field or reservoir engineer
steps.body: Entry-level work is often field-based (drilling, completions, production) before moving into reservoir or reservoir-simulation roles.

steps.title: 4. FE exam early, then PE licensure
steps.body: Fundamentals of Engineering exam right after graduation, then Professional Engineer licensure after ~4 years of work experience, required for senior technical sign-off roles.

steps.title: 5. Track the commodity cycle
steps.body: Pay and hiring move with oil and gas prices; operator-side roles typically pay more than service-company roles, and relocation to basins like the Permian is often part of the career.

tools: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) membership and journals
pitfalls: Entering right before a commodity downturn, hiring and pay in this field are cyclical, not steady
Underestimating how geographically concentrated the job market is
Treating this as a 'safe' long-term bet without watching the energy transition's effect on long-run headcount, BLS projects only 1% growth here, the flattest in this batch

pharmacists.headline: Play pharmacists: license once, then pick clinical over retail
pharmacists.whoItsFor: People who want a defined, four-year clinical doctorate with a fairly compressed, predictable pay band, not a path to outsized upside.
pharmacists.firstDollar: ~8 years to first income as a licensed PharmD; retail employment has softened, so clinical and hospital residency tracks are increasingly where the job growth is.

steps.title: 1. Pre-pharmacy coursework
steps.body: 2+ years of prerequisite science courses, many students complete these within a bachelor's, some programs accept after 2 years of undergrad.

steps.title: 2. PCAT (where required) and PharmCAS application
steps.body: Fewer PharmD programs still require the PCAT, check each target program, and apply through the centralized PharmCAS system.

steps.title: 3. PharmD program (4 years)
steps.body: Doctor of Pharmacy degree from an ACPE-accredited school, including Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience (APPE) rotations in the final year.

steps.title: 4. Pass licensure exams
steps.body: NAPLEX (national) and MPJE (state-specific pharmacy law) are both required to practice.

steps.title: 5. Choose retail/community vs. clinical
steps.body: Retail chains hire straight out of licensure; hospital and clinical specialty roles often require a 1-2 year residency (PGY1/PGY2) but pay more and are the growing side of the field.

pitfalls: PharmD debt loads that are high relative to a fairly compressed pay band, unlike medicine, there is no six-figure jump waiting at the top
Chasing retail hours that are shrinking as chains cut pharmacist staffing
Skipping a residency when targeting clinical/hospital roles that increasingly expect one

aerospace-engineers.headline: Play aerospace engineers: one degree, defense or commercial space
aerospace-engineers.whoItsFor: Engineering students who want a fast, single-bachelor's on-ramp into aircraft, spacecraft, or defense systems work.
aerospace-engineers.firstDollar: ~4 years. A first job out of an ABET-accredited aerospace engineering bachelor's pays well above the general engineering median.

steps.title: 1. ABET-accredited aerospace/aeronautical engineering bachelor's
steps.body: Core coursework in aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, and controls; co-ops or internships during school are the standard hiring pipeline.

steps.title: 2. Target defense primes or commercial aviation/space
steps.body: Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Northrop Grumman, and RTX hire the bulk of the field; SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Relativity are the fast-growing commercial-space alternative.

steps.title: 3. Get clearance-eligible if going defense
steps.body: Many defense-prime roles require or strongly prefer U.S. citizenship and eligibility for a security clearance; this can gate which teams you're placed on.

steps.title: 4. Specialize early
steps.body: Propulsion, structures, avionics/controls, or systems engineering are the common sub-tracks; commercial space companies especially reward generalist engineers who can move fast across disciplines.

steps.title: 5. PE licensure or a master's for senior tracks
steps.body: Not required for most industry roles, but a master's (often employer-funded) or PE licensure supports the move into senior or principal engineer roles.

pitfalls: Assuming defense and commercial space pay and hire the same way, clearance requirements, program funding cycles, and equity upside all differ sharply
Treating the degree as terminal without specializing into a sub-discipline hiring managers actually screen for
Underestimating how cyclical defense-program funding can be for job stability

physician-assistants.headline: Play physician assistants: the fastest clinical six-figure track
physician-assistants.whoItsFor: People who want real clinical scope of practice, exam, diagnose, prescribe, without the decade-plus MD/DO runway.
physician-assistants.firstDollar: ~7 years to first income as a licensed PA; roughly half the time-to-income of physicians-surgeons, the fastest path to a clinical six-figure salary in this batch.

steps.title: 1. Bachelor's + healthcare hours
steps.body: Most PA programs require prerequisite science coursework plus direct patient-care experience (often 1,000+ hours) as an EMT, CNA, medical scribe, or similar before you can apply.

steps.title: 2. Apply through CASPA
steps.body: The centralized PA school application system; competitive programs weigh GPA, patient-care hours, and the GRE (where required) heavily.

steps.title: 3. PA program (master's, ~2-3 years)
steps.body: Accredited by ARC-PA, includes classroom science plus clinical rotations across specialties like surgery, primary care, and emergency medicine.

steps.title: 4. Pass the PANCE
steps.body: The Physician Assistant National Certifying Exam is the single licensure gate; pass it, get a state license, and you can practice.

steps.title: 5. Choose a specialty and setting
steps.body: Unlike physicians, PAs can move between specialties without redoing residency; surgical and high-acuity specialties pay above the median, primary care and outpatient settings pay closer to it.

tools: PANCE prep (Rosh Review, PANCE Prep Pearls)
pitfalls: Underestimating the patient-care-hours prerequisite, this alone can add a year or two before you can even apply
Picking a program based on acceptance rate alone without checking PANCE first-time pass rates
Assuming specialty mobility is unlimited, moving into surgical subspecialties still requires on-the-job training even without a new residency

nurse-practitioners.headline: Play nurse practitioner: RN to APRN, the highest-ceiling nursing path
nurse-practitioners.whoItsFor: RNs (or pre-nursing students) willing to commit 6-8 years of school and clinicals for one of the best-paying, fastest-growing licensed roles in healthcare.
nurse-practitioners.firstDollar: RN wages start after the BSN (~4 yrs); full NP-level pay starts after the MSN/DNP and board certification (~6-8 yrs total).

steps.title: 1. Get the BSN and RN license
steps.body: Accredited BSN program (or ADN-to-BSN bridge), then pass the NCLEX-RN. This is your earning floor while you train further.

steps.title: 2. Work as an RN and pick a track
steps.body: 1-2 years of bedside RN experience strengthens grad-school applications and clarifies family, acute care, psych, or CRNA.

steps.title: 3. Complete the MSN or DNP
steps.body: Accredited nurse practitioner program, in-person or hybrid, with clinical hours logged under a preceptor.

steps.title: 4. Pass national certification and get licensed
steps.body: ANCC or AANP boards depending on track; state APRN license and, where required, a collaborative practice agreement.

steps.title: 5. Negotiate scope and setting
steps.body: Full-practice-authority states let you run your own clinic; CRNA and specialty tracks push pay well past the $132K median.

pitfalls: Choosing an unaccredited or diploma-mill NP program
Skipping bedside RN experience before grad school
Not checking your state's scope-of-practice rules before committing to a specialty

actuaries.headline: Play actuary: pass exams, climb from analyst to Fellow
actuaries.whoItsFor: Math and stats-strong people who want steady six-figure pay without patient contact or sales, and don't mind years of professional exams.
actuaries.firstDollar: Entry-level actuarial analyst roles pay while you sit for exams; full Fellow-level pay (FSA/FCAS) takes roughly 6-10 years.

steps.title: 1. Build the math base
steps.body: Bachelor's in math, statistics, actuarial science, or a related quantitative field; strong Excel, SQL, and R help.

steps.title: 2. Pass 1-2 exams before you're hired
steps.body: SOA (Exams P, FM) or CAS (Exams 1, 2). Passing even one before graduating is the biggest lever on landing an entry role.

steps.title: 3. Land an entry-level actuarial analyst job
steps.body: Insurers, consultancies, and reinsurers hire actuarial trainees who study on paid company time.

steps.title: 4. Keep passing exams on a schedule
steps.body: ASA/ACAS status after roughly 7 exams, FSA/FCAS after the full sequence. Each pass typically triggers a raise.

steps.title: 5. Specialize for the ceiling
steps.body: Health, life, P&C, or pension track; chief actuary and consulting-partner roles clear $200K-$300K+.

pitfalls: Failing to pass any exams before applying, which makes cold-hiring much harder
Picking the SOA vs CAS track without checking which employers you actually want
Burning out by cramming exams instead of pacing 1-2 a year

data-scientists.headline: Play data scientist: stats plus software, ride the analytics boom
data-scientists.whoItsFor: People comfortable with both statistics and code who want to build models and analysis pipelines, with a shorter path than a PhD-track research role.
data-scientists.firstDollar: Entry analyst or DS roles are reachable in about 1-2 years with the right portfolio; the strongest offers cluster around bachelor's-plus-experience or a master's.

steps.title: 1. Learn the actual stack
steps.body: Python (pandas, scikit-learn), SQL, statistics through regression and hypothesis testing, and one visualization tool.

steps.title: 2. Build projects on real data
steps.body: End-to-end projects, ingest, clean, model, ship a result, beat Kaggle-only portfolios. Publish them on GitHub.

steps.title: 3. Get a foot-in role
steps.body: Data analyst or junior DS role to build production experience; a master's helps but isn't mandatory with a strong portfolio.

steps.title: 4. Ship models that move a metric
steps.body: Employers promote people who can tie a model to revenue, cost, or retention, not just an accuracy score.

steps.title: 5. Specialize toward ML engineering or leadership
steps.body: MLOps/ML engineering tracks toward big-tech comp; management track toward analytics leadership.

pitfalls: Portfolio full of tutorial clones instead of original analysis
Chasing every new ML framework instead of shipping
Ignoring communication, since models nobody understands don't get used

financial-investment-analysts.headline: Play financial analyst: model, cover, and climb toward the buy side
financial-investment-analysts.whoItsFor: Finance, econ, or math grads who want structured corporate or Wall Street pay with a clear promotion ladder, and are willing to grind modeling reps early.
financial-investment-analysts.firstDollar: Analyst-level pay starts right out of undergrad; the CFA and buy-side or quant moves are what push past the $101K median.

steps.title: 1. Get the base degree
steps.body: Finance, economics, accounting, or, for quant tracks, math, statistics, or CS.

steps.title: 2. Land an analyst seat
steps.body: Corporate FP&A, equity research, or an IB analyst program. Recruiting is relationship- and internship-driven, so start early.

steps.title: 3. Start the CFA if you're staying analyst-side
steps.body: Level I is common to sit for while still working; the full charter (3 levels, roughly 2-4 years) is the credential that signals seriousness.

steps.title: 4. Build a modeling and market track record
steps.body: DCFs, comps, real calls you made. This is your pitch for a buy-side or research move.

steps.title: 5. Move toward the ceiling
steps.body: Hedge fund, private equity, or quant research roles pay multiples of the BLS median but sit in the top tail, not the base case.

tools: Wall Street Prep or similar course
pitfalls: Treating the CFA as a substitute for real deal and modeling experience
Assuming top-tail hedge-fund pay is the median outcome
Networking only after you need a job, not before

welder-fabricator.headline: Play welder: certify fast, then chase the pay in the specialty
welder-fabricator.whoItsFor: Hands-on people who want one of the shortest training-to-paycheck trades, with a real path to six figures through rig, pipeline, or underwater specialization.
welder-fabricator.firstDollar: 6 months to 2 years through a welding program or apprenticeship gets you a first paycheck; specialty certs unlock the higher tiers.

steps.title: 1. Learn the core processes
steps.body: Stick, MIG, TIG, and flux-core through a community college or trade school program, or a shop apprenticeship.

steps.title: 2. Pass AWS certification tests
steps.body: Certified welder tests, per process and position, are what employers and unions actually check, not just the class.

steps.title: 3. Take entry shop or construction work
steps.body: Build plate and pipe reps, speed, and a clean visual or x-ray pass rate.

steps.title: 4. Specialize for the pay jump
steps.body: Pipeline (travel-heavy), structural or rig, or underwater (adds commercial dive school at $15K-$30K) all pay well above the shop-welder median.

steps.title: 5. Own the equipment if you go independent
steps.body: A welding truck or rig ($40K-$100K) lets you contract directly instead of through a shop.

tools: welding truck or rig for independent work
pitfalls: Certifying in only one process or position and getting boxed out of jobs
Underestimating the travel demands of pipeline and rig work
Skipping dive-school prerequisites before chasing underwater rates

elevator-escalator-installer.headline: Play elevator mechanic: the highest-paid trade with the tightest door
elevator-escalator-installer.whoItsFor: People willing to compete hard for a limited number of NEIEP/IUEC apprenticeship slots, in exchange for one of the best trade-only median wages in the country.
elevator-escalator-installer.firstDollar: Apprentice wages start once you're accepted; full mechanic pay ($106K median) hits after the 4-5 year apprenticeship.

steps.title: 1. Check eligibility and apply early
steps.body: NEIEP, the IUEC's training arm, posts openings by local; slots are few and applications often open only occasionally.

steps.title: 2. Pass the aptitude test and interview
steps.body: Mechanical aptitude testing plus an interview; a construction, trade, or military background helps your odds.

steps.title: 3. Complete the 4-5 year apprenticeship
steps.body: Paid on-the-job training under a mechanic plus NEIEP coursework, covering hydraulics, traction systems, and controls.

steps.title: 4. License and certify per state
steps.body: Many states require a separate elevator mechanic license or exam on top of the apprenticeship.

steps.title: 5. Work toward a service route or adjuster role
steps.body: Service mechanics on a set route, and adjusters who commission new installs, sit at the top of the pay band.

pitfalls: Assuming you can start without going through NEIEP/IUEC, since most of the market is unionized
Underestimating how few slots open each year; plan a backup trade while you wait

electrical-power-line-installer.headline: Play lineman: apprenticeship first, storm work pays the ceiling
electrical-power-line-installer.whoItsFor: People who want top trade pay, can pass a physical/climbing test, and will travel for storm work.
electrical-power-line-installer.firstDollar: Apprentice wages from day one of a paid 3-4 yr program; lineman school grads still need an apprenticeship before full journeyman pay.

steps.title: 1. Choose the path
steps.body: Lineman school (15wk-15mo) for a resume edge, or apply direct to a utility/IBEW apprenticeship (3-4 yr paid, no school debt).

steps.title: 2. Pass the gate tests
steps.body: CDL, DOT physical, pole-climb and aptitude tests (EEI TECH/CAST). Utilities and IBEW locals screen hard before hiring.

steps.title: 3. Log apprentice hours safely
steps.body: OJT under journeymen, classroom code hours, arc-flash and climbing safety certs. Mistakes at height are fatal, the culture is strict for a reason.

steps.title: 4. Chase storm and travel work
steps.body: Mutual-aid deployments and overtime after hurricanes/ice storms are how journeymen clear $120K-$150K+, not base rate alone.

steps.title: 5. Specialize or go contractor
steps.body: Substation vs transmission vs distribution, or move into a line-crew foreman/contracting role for the next ceiling.

pitfalls: skipping physical/climb screen prep and washing out
treating lineman school as a guarantee of a union slot

dental-hygienist.headline: Play dental hygienist: high hourly pay, ownership blocked in most states
dental-hygienist.whoItsFor: People who want strong pay-per-hour healthcare work without dental school debt, willing to check the law before assuming they can own a practice.
dental-hygienist.firstDollar: Months after finishing the associate program and passing boards; most start as a W-2 hire in a private practice.

steps.title: 1. Finish an accredited program
steps.body: 2-3 yr CODA-accredited associate degree with clinical hours.

steps.title: 2. Pass boards and license
steps.body: National/regional written exam + state clinical exam + state license application.

steps.title: 3. Work the employee track first
steps.body: Private-practice pay-per-hour is the real ceiling lever; negotiate day rate, not just hourly.

steps.title: 4. Check your state's ownership law
steps.body: Most states legally bar hygienists from owning a practice; CO (proprietorship), ME (IPDH), and CA (RDHAP) are exceptions.

steps.title: 5. Go independent only where it's legal
steps.body: Build direct-access clientele (nursing homes, schools, underserved patients) under that state's specific supervision rules.

pitfalls: assuming ownership is legal in your state without checking first
underpricing independent-practice visits relative to a dental office
not negotiating day rate as an employee

locksmith.headline: Play locksmith: lowest capital in the trades, emergency premium pays the bills
locksmith.whoItsFor: People who want a fast, cheap start and don't mind after-hours lockout calls.
locksmith.firstDollar: Often within weeks: first paid lockout or rekey job once tools and licensing (where required) are sorted.

steps.title: 1. Get trained fast
steps.body: Weeks-to-months of hands-on training via community college, ALOA courses, or apprenticing under a working locksmith.

steps.title: 2. Check your state's license/bond rules
steps.body: Requirements vary widely, some states require licensing and background checks, others none. Get compliant before advertising.

steps.title: 3. Buy the minimum kit
steps.body: Key machine, pick/bypass tools, a service vehicle. Realistic startup is ~$5K-$20K, among the cheapest trade launches.

steps.title: 4. Price the emergency premium
steps.body: After-hours lockouts and automotive transponder work carry the real margin; a bare rekey call barely covers overhead.

steps.title: 5. Build local visibility
steps.body: Google Business Profile and local SEO matter more than brand, most working locksmiths are self-employed and invisible to BLS.

pitfalls: no way to verify a caller's right to the property, a real liability exposure

appliance-repair-technician.headline: Play appliance repair: van, parts markup, and diagnosis speed
appliance-repair-technician.whoItsFor: People who like mechanical/electrical troubleshooting and want a low-barrier owner-operator route.
appliance-repair-technician.firstDollar: Often within weeks of training/certs: first paid service call once you have a van and basic tool kit.

steps.title: 1. Get trained
steps.body: Weeks to a few months via manufacturer certs, a community college program, or working under an established tech.

steps.title: 2. Get EPA 608 if you'll touch sealed refrigeration
steps.body: Required for fridge/freezer and other sealed-system repair work.

steps.title: 3. Stock the van
steps.body: Common parts inventory (belts, igniters, control boards, seals) cuts callback trips and lifts close rate.

steps.title: 4. Price the callout plus parts markup
steps.body: The diagnostic fee covers the drive; parts markup and labor are where the real margin sits.

steps.title: 5. Add techs once booked solid
steps.body: Single-tech owners commonly clear ~$75K; 3-5 techs scale toward $150K-$200K+ EBITDA.

pitfalls: no parts inventory causing dead return trips
scaling to multiple techs before dispatch/booking systems exist

twitch-live-streaming.headline: Play Twitch: thousands of unpaid hours before any real money
twitch-live-streaming.whoItsFor: People who can stream 20-40+ hrs/week live, tolerate zero pay for a long stretch, and bring real charisma or a competitive skill edge.
twitch-live-streaming.firstDollar: First subs/donations can land within ~6 months, but a livable income never arrives for the vast majority of streamers.

steps.title: 1. Pick a discoverable format
steps.body: Choose a game or format with real concurrent-viewer discoverability on Twitch, not just your personal favorite.

steps.title: 2. Stream on a real schedule
steps.body: 4-6 days/week, same time slot, for months before judging traction. Consistency is how the algorithm and viewers both learn you exist.

steps.title: 3. Network inside the community
steps.body: Raids, collabs, and Discord presence matter more than Twitch's own discovery, which is weak for small channels.

steps.title: 4. Convert viewers into subs
steps.body: Give people a clear reason to return: personality, banter, a recognizable format. Views without retention don't monetize.

steps.title: 5. Move past platform payouts
steps.body: Once you have real concurrent viewers, sponsorships and direct deals pay far more than Twitch's own sub/bit payouts.

pitfalls: Burnout from unpaid 40+ hour weeks with no guaranteed return
Chasing sub count instead of building an actual community
Treating Twitch payouts as the ceiling when sponsorships are the real money
No backup income during the multi-month zero-revenue stretch

podcasting.headline: Play podcasting: downloads compound slowly, ad money is gated on scale
podcasting.whoItsFor: People who can commit to a weekly cadence for 1-2+ years before ad money is real; easier with an existing audience or a co-host who brings distribution.
podcasting.firstDollar: Around 2 years to real income. Ad money meaningfully starts near the ~10,000 downloads/episode threshold, which very few shows reach.

steps.title: 1. Pick a sustainable format
steps.body: Interview, solo, or co-host, whichever you can actually sustain weekly without burning out.

steps.title: 2. Publish consistently before monetizing
steps.body: 6-12 months minimum. Downloads compound slowly and most podfade happens before episode 10.

steps.title: 3. Fix production quality early
steps.body: Bad audio loses new listeners in the first minute. Editing and show notes are not optional polish, they're retention.

steps.title: 4. Hit the ad threshold
steps.body: Once downloads approach ~10K/episode, start dynamic ad insertion or direct sponsor outreach. Below that, ad money is negligible.

steps.title: 5. Layer memberships and cross-promotion
steps.body: Patreon/memberships plus guest-audience cross-promotion keep the download count compounding past the ad threshold.

pitfalls: Quitting before episode 20, where most podfade happens
Recording quality bad enough to lose new listeners immediately
Chasing celebrity guests before there's an audience to justify their time

app-development.headline: Play app development: ship a niche app, fight the store lottery
app-development.whoItsFor: Engineers who can ship fast and iterate on ASO and retention, not just write code.
app-development.firstDollar: Weeks after launch with paid UA or a viral loop; most solo apps never clear $1,000/mo.

steps.title: 1. Pick a narrow, painful niche
steps.body: Chase one underserved use case, not a broad everything-app. Subscriptions need obvious recurring value.

steps.title: 2. Ship an MVP in weeks
steps.body: One core loop, a working paywall on day one. Flutter/React Native/Swift, whichever you can ship fastest.

steps.title: 3. Nail App Store Optimization
steps.body: Title, screenshots, keywords, and reviews decide if anyone finds you before you write a line of ad copy.

steps.title: 4. Test paid UA on a tight budget
steps.body: TikTok/Meta ads to find a payback period that works before scaling spend. Kill what doesn't convert.

steps.title: 5. Iterate on retention and pricing
steps.body: Most solo apps die from churn, not lack of downloads. A/B test onboarding and the paywall relentlessly.

tools: App Store Connect / Google Play Console
pitfalls: Building a broad app nobody searches for
Ignoring ASO and hoping for organic discovery
Scaling ad spend before the payback period is proven

real-estate-agent-broker.headline: Play real estate agent: license fast, then build a repeat-client machine
real-estate-agent-broker.whoItsFor: People good with strangers who can survive commission-only income during the first slow months.
real-estate-agent-broker.firstDollar: Weeks after licensing, but the true first close often takes 2-4 months of prospecting.

steps.title: 1. Get licensed
steps.body: State pre-license course plus exam, typically weeks and $1-2K. Join a brokerage that actually trains new agents.

steps.title: 2. Pick a farm
steps.body: A neighborhood, price band, or niche (first-time buyers, relocations, luxury) you can dominate instead of chasing every lead.

steps.title: 3. Build a pipeline beyond Zillow leads
steps.body: Sphere of influence, open houses, referral partners (lenders, attorneys), and consistent follow-up beat paid leads alone.

steps.title: 4. Systemize the transaction
steps.body: Checklists, a transaction coordinator once you can afford one, and a CRM so no lead or deadline slips.

steps.title: 5. Convert closings into referrals
steps.body: Past clients should eventually outproduce new-lead prospecting; this is how top producers scale far past the median.

pitfalls: Underestimating the cash runway needed before the first commission lands
Chasing every lead source instead of owning one farm
No systemized follow-up, deals go cold

recruiter-staffing-agency.headline: Play recruiting: get paid on placement, then build a desk
recruiter-staffing-agency.whoItsFor: People who like sourcing and sales, comfortable on the phone, patient with a commission-based ramp.
recruiter-staffing-agency.firstDollar: Weeks to a first placement fee once you have live requisitions and a working candidate pipeline.

steps.title: 1. Pick a niche you can source in
steps.body: Vertical (healthcare, tech, skilled trades) or role type. Generalist desks lose to specialists on both sides of the placement.

steps.title: 2. Land your first client reqs
steps.body: Cold outreach to hiring managers, or join an agency to learn the model on someone else's book of business first.

steps.title: 3. Build a real sourcing pipeline
steps.body: Boolean search, LinkedIn Recruiter, referrals, and a database you own, not just job board scraping.

steps.title: 4. Run a tight interview-to-offer process
steps.body: Fast screens, honest expectation-setting on both sides, constant candidate communication cuts fall-off.

steps.title: 5. Go solo or scale a team
steps.body: Once you have a repeatable placement rate, decide between staying a high-earning solo desk or hiring recruiters under you.

pitfalls: Generalist desk with no niche edge
No owned candidate database, starting from zero every search
Placing candidates who don't stick past the guarantee period

fractional-cfo-bookkeeping.headline: Play fractional finance: bookkeeping first, CFO leverage later
fractional-cfo-bookkeeping.whoItsFor: People with real accounting or finance chops who want recurring B2B revenue instead of one employer.
fractional-cfo-bookkeeping.firstDollar: Weeks to months for a first retainer client, faster with an existing SMB or startup network.

steps.title: 1. Start where the barrier is lowest
steps.body: Bookkeeping needs no license. Get 2-3 small-business clients on monthly retainer to build cash flow and case studies.

steps.title: 2. Get the stack right
steps.body: QuickBooks/Xero certification signals competence fast to non-finance-savvy owners.

steps.title: 3. Ladder into fractional CFO work
steps.body: Once you have books-level trust, upsell forecasting, cash runway, and fundraise-readiness work at CFO rates.

steps.title: 4. Price as a retainer, not by the hour
steps.body: A recurring monthly fee scoped to deliverables (close, reporting, board deck) protects margin as you add clients.

steps.title: 5. Cap client count deliberately
steps.body: A handful of well-paying retainers beats a dozen thin ones; protect the hours that let you charge CFO rates.

pitfalls: Underpricing bookkeeping and staying stuck there
Taking on clients with no clean books to start from
No written scope, retainer creeps into unpaid CFO work

social-media-management.headline: Play SMM: productize a niche retainer
social-media-management.whoItsFor: Platform-fluent operators who'd rather manage brand content than build their own audience.
social-media-management.firstDollar: Weeks via outbound to local or niche brands with a tight portfolio.

steps.title: 1. Pick a platform and niche
steps.body: Instagram for restaurants, LinkedIn for B2B founders. One lane beats 'I do all social.'

steps.title: 2. Build a spec portfolio
steps.body: Mock up a week of content for a dream client, unpaid, to show the work not just talk about it.

steps.title: 3. Land the first retainer
steps.body: Local businesses and small brands first; DM outreach with the spec work attached.

steps.title: 4. Systematize the pipeline
steps.body: Content calendar, approval flow, monthly report. Batch-create, don't live inside the feed.

steps.title: 5. Raise rates or add scope
steps.body: Ads management, UGC sourcing, or a second niche once one retainer is proven.

pitfalls: pricing by post instead of retainer
no reporting so clients cannot see value

seo-freelance.headline: Play SEO: proof beats promises
seo-freelance.whoItsFor: Technical and content operators who can show a real ranking, not just describe a strategy.
seo-freelance.firstDollar: Months; case studies from your own or a friend's site come before paid clients.

steps.title: 1. Rank one site first
steps.body: Your own blog, a friend's business, anything. A real result beats a certification.

steps.title: 2. Package a tight offer
steps.body: Technical audit, content plan, or link building. Not 'full-service SEO' on day one.

steps.title: 3. Target B2B and local
steps.body: Higher retainer tolerance than consumer content sites.

steps.title: 4. Report against dollars, not just rankings
steps.body: Traffic and rank tell a story; leads and revenue close renewals.

steps.title: 5. Adapt to AI search
steps.body: Citation-worthy, structured content matters alongside classic technical SEO now.

pitfalls: selling rankings with no revenue story
content-only work with no technical audit

no-code-web-agency.headline: Play no-code: speed is the pitch
no-code-web-agency.whoItsFor: Tool-fluent builders with taste who can ship a client site in days, not months.
no-code-web-agency.firstDollar: Weeks; first project from a warm network or a portfolio piece done on spec.

steps.title: 1. Pick one stack
steps.body: Webflow, Framer, or Bubble. Depth in one beats shallow fluency in three.

steps.title: 2. Build 2-3 portfolio pieces
steps.body: Redesign a real brand's site on spec if you have zero client work yet.

steps.title: 3. Sell fixed packages
steps.body: Landing page, 5-page site, light app. Fixed price and scope, not hourly.

steps.title: 4. Templatize your process
steps.body: Reusable components and a build checklist cut delivery time each project.

steps.title: 5. Ladder into retainers
steps.body: Hosting, updates, and CRO become recurring revenue after the build.

pitfalls: endless revisions with no scope line
racing to the bottom on Fiverr/Upwork

tiktok-shop-social-commerce.headline: Play TikTok Shop: the video is the storefront
tiktok-shop-social-commerce.whoItsFor: Content-first operators comfortable filming daily and sourcing or picking products fast.
tiktok-shop-social-commerce.firstDollar: Weeks after a first algorithm-favored post with an in-feed product link.

steps.title: 1. Pick a product lane
steps.body: Source your own, dropship, or join an affiliate program. Margin after returns is the real number.

steps.title: 2. Post daily in-feed content
steps.body: Demos, unboxings, before/after. Volume and hooks beat production value.

steps.title: 3. Get into the Shop tab
steps.body: Set up the TikTok Shop seller account, listings, and shipping before you scale content.

steps.title: 4. Watch returns and margin
steps.body: Impulse-buy traffic returns more than intentional shoppers; price for it.

steps.title: 5. Diversify off one platform
steps.body: Repost winners to Instagram/YouTube Shorts; algorithm risk can zero a channel overnight.

pitfalls: ignoring return rates on impulse buys
chasing virality with no margin behind it

domain-flipping.headline: Play domain flipping: buy taste, sell patience
domain-flipping.whoItsFor: People with spare capital and a real eye for brandable or aged names. Not a cash-now path; treat it like an illiquid side portfolio.
domain-flipping.firstDollar: Months to a year. Most domains sit unsold; budget for dead capital and slow sales cycles.

steps.title: 1. Pick one lane
steps.body: Brandables, aged expired-domain drops, or niche keyword domains. Do not spread across all three at once.

steps.title: 2. Buy on the aftermarket
steps.body: GoDaddy Auctions, NameJet, Dynadot marketplace, expired-domain drop catches beat fresh registrations for resale value.

steps.title: 3. List everywhere buyers look
steps.body: Afternic, Sedo, Dan.com, plus your own for-sale landers with a clear buy-it-now price.

steps.title: 4. Price to actually sell
steps.body: Check comps on similar names sold recently. Negotiate a real offer instead of holding out for a home run.

steps.title: 5. Reinvest gradually
steps.body: Roll early wins into 2-3 more names. Do not put the whole float into one big bet.

pitfalls: Overpaying on gut feeling with no comps
Registering fresh generic names nobody searches for
Treating a domain portfolio as a retirement plan instead of a side bet

online-tutoring.headline: Play online tutoring: rate over platform
online-tutoring.whoItsFor: People with real subject mastery (test prep, language, STEM) who want cash fast with zero capital.
online-tutoring.firstDollar: Weeks. Sign up, get your first trial lesson booked.

steps.title: 1. Pick a scarce subject
steps.body: MCAT/LSAT prep, advanced math, or a credentialed language beats generic homework help on rate.

steps.title: 2. Start on a platform for reviews
steps.body: Preply, Wyzant, iTalki. Underprice your first 5-10 lessons to bank five-star ratings fast.

steps.title: 3. Raise your rate on a schedule
steps.body: Every 10 five-star reviews, raise price. Tutors who stall at intro pricing cap their own ceiling.

steps.title: 4. Move top clients direct
steps.body: Once trust is built, offer a discount off the platform fee for direct payment, checking platform terms first.

steps.title: 5. Package for volume
steps.body: Group classes or a small cohort course once you have a repeat roster. Hourly 1:1 alone caps your income.

pitfalls: Platform-only with no owned channel or repeat-client base
No niche, so you compete purely on price

bug-bounty-security.headline: Play bug bounty: methodology beats luck
bug-bounty-security.whoItsFor: Security-skilled builders who can go deep on one vuln class instead of spraying every program. Power-law payouts; most accounts earn near zero.
bug-bounty-security.firstDollar: Months, if ever. Budget a year of largely unpaid learning before the first real bounty lands.

steps.title: 1. Learn on labs first
steps.body: PortSwigger Web Security Academy, HackTheBox, TryHackMe before touching a live program.

steps.title: 2. Specialize in one vuln class
steps.body: IDOR, SSRF, auth bypass. Depth on one class beats shallow breadth across all of them.

steps.title: 3. Pick programs with real payout history
steps.body: HackerOne and Bugcrowd leaderboards show which programs actually pay out at meaningful severity.

steps.title: 4. Write reports that get triaged fast
steps.body: Clear repro steps, real impact, a fix suggestion. Sloppy reports get closed as N/A regardless of the bug.

steps.title: 5. Build a public track record
steps.body: Write-ups and CTF placings get you invited to private programs and paid pentest contracts, the real income ladder.

pitfalls: Chasing every program with no specialty
Treating this as full income before month one of real payouts exists

faceless-content-automation.headline: Play faceless content: defensible niche first, avoid the copyright trap
faceless-content-automation.whoItsFor: Editors who can produce consistent volume without appearing on camera. Crowded meta; most channels never monetize.
faceless-content-automation.firstDollar: 12-18 months of consistent uploads before YouTube Partner Program or sponsor money is real.

steps.title: 1. Pick a defensible niche
steps.body: Narrated documentaries, original compilations, or properly licensed footage, not reuploaded clips.

steps.title: 2. Build a repeatable pipeline
steps.body: Script, voice, edit, thumbnail. Know your real cost per video before you scale upload volume.

steps.title: 3. Upload on a real schedule for months
steps.body: The algorithm needs a consistent signal, not a burst. Judge results at month 6-12, not week 2.

steps.title: 4. Clear the monetization gates
steps.body: YPP watch-hour and subscriber thresholds first, then layer AdSense, sponsorships, and affiliate links.

steps.title: 5. Diversify beyond one channel
steps.body: Spread the niche across a second channel or platform so one copyright strike does not zero you out.

pitfalls: Reused footage that gets copyright-struck or demonetized
Chasing view count with no monetization plan
Quitting before month 12, when most channels are still near zero

paid-surveys-microtasks.headline: Play surveys and microtasks: pocket money, not a plan
paid-surveys-microtasks.whoItsFor: Anyone who wants a few dollars for spare minutes. Nobody should build an income plan around this deck; it is on the board to keep the meta honest.
paid-surveys-microtasks.firstDollar: Minutes. Sign up, complete a task, get paid same day or week.

steps.title: 1. Stack 2-3 legit platforms
steps.body: Prolific, UserTesting, and Amazon Mechanical Turk pay better per hour than generic survey panels.

steps.title: 2. Filter for the highest-paying task types
steps.body: User testing and screened research studies pay far more per hour than click-through surveys.

steps.title: 3. Track your real hourly rate
steps.body: Log time against payout for a week. Most people quit once they see the true number.

steps.title: 4. Treat payouts as beer money
steps.body: Do not count on this for rent, bills, or as a savings plan. The win rate is the whole problem with this deck.

steps.title: 5. Use it as a bridge, not a destination
steps.body: If you have any real skill, move to freelancing or online tutoring the moment you can land one paying client.

tools: A spreadsheet to track real hourly rate
pitfalls: Mistaking gross payouts for livable income
Sinking hours other decks would pay 10x for
Panels that pay in gift cards or points instead of cash

email-marketing-service.headline: Play email marketing: sell the lift, not the hours
email-marketing-service.whoItsFor: Writers who understand ecommerce or SaaS funnels and can point to a real revenue lift, not just good copy.
email-marketing-service.firstDollar: Weeks to a first retainer if you already know one ESP well and can show a before/after metric.

steps.title: 1. Master one ESP deeply
steps.body: Klaviyo for ecommerce or Customer.io/HubSpot for SaaS. Deep specialist beats broad-but-shallow.

steps.title: 2. Build 2-3 proof pieces
steps.body: Audit an existing brand's flows for free or cheap, document the fix and the measured lift.

steps.title: 3. Price the retainer on flows and campaigns
steps.body: Welcome, abandon cart, post-purchase, and win-back is a sellable fixed-scope package, not an hourly quote.

steps.title: 4. Report the number that matters
steps.body: Email-attributed revenue as a percent of total revenue, pulled from the client's own dashboard.

steps.title: 5. Ladder into an agency
steps.body: Once you have 3-5 retainer clients, hire a second copywriter and take a cut instead of trading more of your own hours.

tools: A swipe file of proven flows
pitfalls: Pricing hourly instead of by outcome
No before/after proof, so every pitch is a cold claim
One-off campaigns instead of recurring flow retainers

stock-media-assets.headline: Play stock media: volume compounds, one upload doesn't
stock-media-assets.whoItsFor: Photographers, videographers, or audio/3D creators willing to build a large catalog over years, not weeks.
stock-media-assets.firstDollar: Months for the first sale; real monthly income needs a catalog in the thousands of assets.

steps.title: 1. Shoot for demand, not personal taste
steps.body: Research what buyers actually license via each platform's trending and bestseller pages before you shoot.

steps.title: 2. Upload to multiple marketplaces at once
steps.body: Shutterstock, Adobe Stock, iStock. Distribution across platforms multiplies the return on a single shoot.

steps.title: 3. Batch metadata and keywords
steps.body: Searchability sells more than raw quality. Spend real time on titles and keywords per asset.

steps.title: 4. Track earnings per platform monthly
steps.body: Drop weak platforms, double down on whichever converts best for your specific niche.

steps.title: 5. Compound the catalog
steps.body: Treat every shoot as permanent inventory. Income lags catalog size by roughly 1-2 years.

tools: Shutterstock / Adobe Stock / iStock contributor accounts
pitfalls: Uploading a few hundred images and expecting real income
Chasing trends instead of evergreen categories

online-bookkeeping-remote.headline: Play remote bookkeeping: certify, niche, retain
online-bookkeeping-remote.whoItsFor: Detail-oriented operators who want a real recurring-revenue service business with a low skill floor and a clear certification path.
online-bookkeeping-remote.firstDollar: Months. QuickBooks Online or Xero certification plus your first 1-2 small-business clients.

steps.title: 1. Get certified on the dominant platform
steps.body: QuickBooks Online ProAdvisor is the credential small-business clients actually check for.

steps.title: 2. Pick an industry niche
steps.body: Ecommerce, med spas, or contractors. Niche bookkeepers command higher rates than generalists.

steps.title: 3. Land the first clients through community
steps.body: Local business Facebook groups, referrals, and nonprofit boards beat cold marketplace bidding.

steps.title: 4. Price as a monthly retainer
steps.body: A fixed monthly fee per client scales your income with your systems, not your hours.

steps.title: 5. Systematize onboarding and close
steps.body: A repeatable checklist per client lets you add clients without adding proportional hours.

pitfalls: No niche, so you compete against $10/hr overseas bids
No systemized month-end close, so growth breaks you
